subject: Admin activity: export formats, provenance, and flexible retention (SOC2/SIG) - Q&A
messages:
From: Anita Cho <anita.cho@sigmahealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@sigmahealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Admin activity evidence — scope + delivery options (SOC 2 / SIG)

Hi Mateo / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we start our SIG assessment I'm compiling the admin activity evidence inventory. To make sure we request the right artifacts from your team, can you confirm the following at a high level:

- Canonical list of admin activity event types you produce (examples: console logins, API keys created/revoked, role/grant changes, artifact pulls, privileged session starts, operator CLI actions).
- Default retention windows for raw vs indexed/admin-summary events and whether those can be extended for a customer-specific retention agreement.
- Export formats you can produce (JSONL, Parquet, CSV) and whether timestamps are normalized to UTC/ISO8601 by default.
- How you provide integrity/provenance: signed manifests, checksums, HMACs, KMS signing, and whether you can supply a chain-of-custody statement.
- Sampling options (e.g., per-user slices, timebox snapshots) and any limits for on-demand exports.

I've attached our questionnaire worksheet to this thread — please populate the 'evidence available' column if possible. We're aiming to include these artifacts in our SOC 2 evidence bundle next month. Ideally we'd get a short writeup and a sample manifest within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Anita Cho
Senior Security Analyst
Sigma Health
[Attachment: sig_questionnaire.xlsx]
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Cho <anita.cho@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence — scope + delivery options (SOC 2 / SIG)

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear list. Short answers here; we'll follow up with a sample manifest and a short export playbook (attachment) by EOD tomorrow.

- Event types: we log (1) user auth events (console/web + SSO token exchanges), (2) API requests (verb, endpoint, caller id, request id), (3) model-inference invocations metadata (request id, model, prompt size — note: we do not retain prompt text by default for hosted customers unless explicitly configured), (4) operator/admin actions (role grants/revokes, policy changes, deployment rollouts, config changes), (5) key management events (KMS operations surfaced as operator actions), (6) privileged session starts/ends and (7) system-level errors/tracebacks tied to request ids for forensic correlation.

- Retention: default retention for raw admin event stream is 180 days. We also maintain an indexed event store (searchable summaries with policy tags) for 1 year. For customers on Dedicated or Private we can negotiate extended retention (e.g., 3 years) as a contract addendum — this requires a reserved-storage commitment.

- Export formats & timestamps: we support JSONL (canonical), Parquet (columnar), and CSV (summary slices). Timestamps are canonicalized to RFC3339/ISO8601 in UTC by default and we include an original-tz field when available.

- Integrity & provenance: exports are accompanied by a signed manifest (SHA-256 checksums for each file + manifest signed using an HMAC whose key is managed in our KMS). For higher assurance we can produce an HMAC plus an attested manifest signed with our audit KMS key and provide a signed PDF chain-of-custody statement that lists the export parameters (timebox, slices, redaction profile). We can also deliver a detached PGP envelope if you require signed-by-customer verification on ingestion.

- Sampling & slices: on-demand exports support arbitrary filters (time window, user IDs, org units, request types). Minimum window for an on-demand export is 1 hour; for very large datasets we recommend using a 24h window for performance. We support per-user slices and tenant-scoped deltas; exports are chunked into 10GB objects for reliable transfer.

Attachments in our follow-up will include: sample-manifest (JSON), export-instructions (Docx), and a short runbook for verifying manifests. If you want a live handoff, we can stage an S3 presigned URL and deliver the set over PGP/GPG.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Redwood Inference]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Cho <anita.cho@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence — scope + delivery options (SOC 2 / SIG)

Anita — two practical clarifications from ops side:

- PII redaction: exports can be delivered in 'raw' or 'scrubbed' modes. Scrubbed removes user-supplied prompt text and masks email local-parts; we can provide a redaction mapping table for review.
- Sampling/limits: for very high-cardinality queries (multi-region, multi-tenant) there is a processing window — bulk on-demand exports started before 18:00 UTC will typically complete within 12-36 hours depending on scope. Emergency snapshot requests (legal/forensic) are prioritized but require verification and a custodian signature.
- Audit key rotation: manifests include the KMS key id used for signing. When we rotate our signing keys we retain old keys in HSM for verification for at least 2 years (attestation available).

If you want, Ben can coordinate a short run through of the sample manifest and verification steps.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Anita Cho <anita.cho@sigmahealth.com>

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick asks before we close the ticket:

1) Can you attach the sample signed manifest and the short export verification doc to this thread (we prefer keeping a copy in our evidence bundle)?
2) Can you confirm the cost/lead time if we request a 3-year retention (contract addendum)? We can loop in procurement on the PO if the cost estimate looks reasonable.

If you can attach the files and a one-paragraph cost estimate by EOD Thursday we should be good. If it's easier to walk through, let's schedule a 30-minute call — I have availability Thu 14:00-16:00 UTC.

Appreciate it,
Anita
Senior Security Analyst, Sigma Health
